title: Legal Basis for Customs Regulatory Authority
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of the legal framework governing customs operations, shifting from the Customs Act, 1969 to the comprehensive Customs Act, 2023. It highlights the transition from specific procedural amendments to the establishment of broad regulatory powers for audits, licensing, and administrative rule-making.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from the 1969 Act to the 2023 Act, reflecting a modernization of customs administrative law.
evolution.scope: Expanded from specific licensing amendments to comprehensive audit and operational authority.

timeline.change: Initial reliance on Customs Act 1969 sections 207 and 219 for licensing rule amendments.
Formal codification of audit powers and legal authority under specific sections of the Customs Act, 1969.
Transition to the Customs Act, 2023 as the primary legal basis for rule-making.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to issue statutory regulatory orders, official directives, and explanatory notices that provide supplementary operational instructions for customs procedures.
